Senses.Explanation: To present an offering is the verb-object rite recorded before an image, at an anniversary, or through burning incense; the first graph does not establish an “upper” or principal rank. Ceremonial headings and regulations place it in an ordered sequence and name the officiating occasion.

A formal teaching-hall address or observance, conventionally headed ‘ascend the hall’ (上堂). Chan turns the ordinary ascent phrase into the standard name of the abbot’s public address and its recorded discourse. It is requested by officials or command, scheduled in monastic codes, announced by placard, delegated to a head monk holding the whisk, suspended and resumed, or introduced by occasion headings. Linji Yixuan’s record separately says officials requested that he take the seat and then records that Linji Yixuan ascended the hall and spoke: the first verb supplies the physical seat-taking while the headword introduces the same formal address event. Headings, requests, scheduling, and verbal narration therefore remain one institutional referent.
Senses.Note: One formal hall-address sense. The former physical split was rejected because its sole line uses a separate verb for taking the seat and the headword for the address. Thirteen witnesses span eleven distinct works.

Senses.Explanation: An established senior is spoken of as already carrying recognized standing and experience. Records use the term collectively for earlier exemplars, for elders sought out by travelling monks, and for living figures whose conduct or words are assessed. It is a status description rather than a personal title tied to one individual.
Senses.Note: The frozen corpus has 2,298 exact hits in 320 files representing 315 works. Eight anchors cover travel to senior teachers, collective reference, criticism, instruction, and historical appraisal. Book-title occurrences alone were excluded.
